result.title: LaVGuard: Selective Decoding for Contextual Value Drift
result.summary: A content-safe response can still promote priorities that conflict with its task: an assistant may demand compliance when asked to preserve autonomy. We study contextual value drift as a task-relative decoding problem with an explicit allowance for change. LaVGuard separates an authorized ten-dimensional profile from a frozen estimate of the values expressed in the visible prefix. A profile-relative density gate selects when to evaluate candidate continuations; their signed progress determines a logit tilt constrained by both changed-position and cumulative-KL budgets. We establish local surrogate improvement, pathwise budget feasibility, and a bound on response-distribution change. Profile conditioning raises boundary TPR at 5% FPR from .58 to .72. At the same .12 mean intervention ratio, the selection study reports risk-safety scores of .88 for LaVGuard and .72 for position-matched edits. The resulting interface makes task priorities actionable while keeping the extent of intervention explicit and bounded.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「情境价值漂移」建模为带显式允许变化的任务相关解码问题：以授权的十维价值 profile 对比冻结的可见前缀价值估计，用密度门控决定何时评估候选续写，并据其有符号进展施加受位置改变与累积 KL 预算约束的 logit 调整，同时给出改进与预算可行性的理论界定。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「门控决定何时干预 + 累积 KL 预算约束的定向扰动」或可供核查 LVR 中按需更新 latent 状态、约束单步改动与停止决策的设计，但属纯文本解码期干预，未涉及视觉证据。
